messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed hovercard numbers in the per-chain cost panel that look off after enabling sampled telemetry for quota-heavy routes. Hover shows negative cache savings for some chains :thinking:
rajiv: oof. can you paste a screenshot? or an example request id? might be sampling bias
maria: quick snippet: chain_id=ch_42, route=/chat/stream, sample_rate=0.01, hovercard shows -$0.03 cache savings per invocation (weird)
tessa: negative savings usually mean our amortization window subtracted warmup cost but sampling made the KV hits look lower. we saw similar with sessionized prefetche before
ben: is this the same flow that uses prefetched_kv_count & batch_warmup_cost in the calc? if sample rate is low, denominator shrinks and noise increases
maria: exactly. hovercard uses estimate: savings = prefetched_tokens * model_unit_cost - warmup_amortized
maria: with sample_rate=0.01 we only have ~10 samples / day for that route, so the estimate is garbage
sophie: two options: 1) suppress hovercard for routes under N samples, 2) surface confidence / CI band instead of a point estimate
rajiv: +1 for confidence band. also maybe add a small CTA: "low sample — view aggregated last 7d" so people don't freak
ben: API change needed though: console currently hits /telemetry/cost/hover?chain=... and returns point estimate. We could extend to return {estimate, count, ci_lower, ci_upper}
rajiv: agree. let's call the param sample_window=7d and include sample_count. naming bikeshed: ci_lower vs lower_bound — prefer standard stats terms
tessa: also need to decide UX for negative values. showing "-" and tooltip explaining can be warmup amortization or small-n noise
maria: can we also take advantage of cached aggregated estimates we compute during daily rollup? that would be less noisy than raw sampled stream
ben: yes, rollup has stable metrics but with 24h lag. propose hybrid: show rollup if sample_count < threshold T, else live estimate
sophie: what's a reasonable T? 50 samples? 100?
rajiv: I'd go 30 for basic sanity, 100 for production confidence. depends on route frequency. make it configurable in the console feature flag
maria: for rollout UX, we need an override: "force live estimate" for debug but default to rollup for low-sample routes
ben: backend: add sample_count and rollup_fallback boolean to the response. console decides. will add telemetry event when user forces live estimate so we can measure usage
tessa: there's also quota interplay: if a tenant has quota throttling, their sample_count might be artificially low and rollup might hide a real regression
sophie: good call. for quota-limited tenants, surface a small banner: "quota may be limiting samples — calculations may be biased"
rajiv: implementation plan:
- api: /telemetry/cost/hover -> include estimate + sample_count + ci + rollup_fallback
- backend: threshold config per org, default 50
- console: show CI band, low-sample CTA, force-live toggle, quota banner
- docs: short note about sampling bias + formula snippet
ben: I'll draft the API PR. thinking about returning precomputed fields to avoid heavy on-the-fly work. maybe add header X-Rollup-Used: true
maria: thanks. can you link the PR when you have a draft? I want to test with canary tenant that had the negative values
ben: will do. starting branch now: WIP/hovercard-sampling
maria: tiny nit: name the flag `hovercard_force_live` in the URL query so we can A/B it per user
rajiv: prefer `force_live_estimate=true` for explicitness
tessa: both fine. we'll standardize in API guide
ops-bot: deploybot: queued deploy of backend/telemetry v2 to canary cluster in 10m :rocket:
maria: perfect, will validate once live. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
